title: The Water Pump — EN/SN/ZU (Mbira Folk)
style: Zimbabwean mbira folk urban grooves acoustic guitar hosho shakers ngoma drums warm baritone 82bpm analog tape warm storytelling Shona Zulu heritage farm memory
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
The water pump sat at the edge of the lower paddock field
Between the cattle trough and the fence that wouldn't yield
You had to prime it twice before it gave up what you needed
The water pump required patience and that message had been heeded

[Verse 2 — Shona, with English translation]
Pombi yemvura yaima pamupendero wemunda
[The water pump stood at the edge of the field]
Yakabatirira mvura, ikaisira zvipfuyo zvose
[It held the water, it gave it to all the cattle]
Wairida kuishandisa kaviri kuitira ishande
[You had to prime it twice to make it work]
Pombi yemvura yakadzidzisa mwoyo kuva wakangwara
[The water pump taught the heart to be patient]

[Chorus — English]
The water pump, the water pump
Standing in the red dust of the African midday
The water pump, the water pump
Everything on the farm flows through it on its way
The water pump knows the drought before we do
The water pump keeps going — that's all we ask it to

[Bridge — Zulu, with English translation]
Ipampu yamanzi yayimi emkhawulweni wensimu
[The water pump stood at the edge of the field]
Yazisa amanzi esilwaneni nasemizini yonke
[It brought water to the animals and all the homes]
Yayidinga ukuhlelwa kabili ngaphambi kokusebenza
[It needed priming twice before working]
Ipampu yamanzi yafundisa ukubekezela
[The water pump taught patience]

[Outro — All three languages]
The water pump knows… Pombi inoziva… Ipampu iyazi
The farm runs on patience — Munda unomhanya nemoyo munyoro — Ipulazi lisebenza ngokunbekezela
The gardens still growing
